blocks.body: A catch basin sits under a grate in the yard or driveway. Runoff falls in, and an outlet pipe partway up the wall carries it to a storm line. Below the outlet is a sump where leaves and grit collect. Clean that sump once a year and the basin keeps working. Let it fill, and debris washes into the outlet and plugs it.

img.alt: Diagram of a catch basin showing the inlet grate, water line, sediment settling in the sump and the outlet pipe carrying water away

blocks.h2: When to Clean an Elmhurst Catch Basin
blocks.body: Fall is the most important time, after the leaves come down on older tree-lined blocks. Spring is the second, after a winter of sand and grit has washed off the driveway. A basin that's half full of silt holds less water and overflows sooner in a heavy rain. A quick check after any big storm, lifting the grate to see how full it is, tells you whether it's time.

blocks.h2: Catch Basin Questions From Elmhurst Homeowners

items.q: How often should a catch basin be cleaned?
items.answer: Every fall, after the leaves come down. Under big trees, spring too.

items.q: Can a blocked basin cause basement water?
items.answer: Yes. Water pooled near the house can seep in or end up in your [sump pump](/elmhurst/sump-pumps) pit.

items.q: Can you rebuild an old brick basin?
items.answer: Often. We rebuild walls and reset grates, or replace it if needed.

items.q: Is the basin in my yard mine to maintain?
items.answer: Usually, if it's on your property and drains your yard.

items.q: Can a catch basin freeze in winter?
items.preview: Yes, if water sits in it.
items.answer: Yes, if water can't drain. Clearing it in fall helps.

items.q: How much does catch basin service cost in Elmhurst?
items.preview: It depends on the work. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on whether it's a cleaning, repair or outlet work. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
